To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
W764C mutation in MSH2 protein complex is predicted to be highly pathogenic and destabilizing.
missense mutations in MSH2- MSH6 protein complex could affect the structural stability and DNA repair mechanism.
the mutation W764C of the MSH6 protein is highly deleterious, destabilizing and affects the DNA repair mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of deleterious and stabilizing missense mutations of MSH2- MSH6 protein complex.
the identification of the pathogenicity and the structural stability of the MSH6-MSH6 interacting residues in the MSH2 protein complex.
the identification of the pathogenic and destabilizing mutations in the MSH2 and MSH6 protein complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the W764C mutation of MSH2 and L1201 F and G1316 E mutations of MSH6 are highly pathogenic and destabilizing in nature.
the W764C mutation in MSH2 could affect the DNA mismatch repair mechanism.
mutations at the interface between MSH2 and MSH6 proteins could have a significant impact on the stability and function of the complex, and hence, on the DNA repair mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the W764C mutation in MSH2 protein is more likely to affect the DNA repair system.
the missense mutations in MSH2 and MSH6 could lead to a higher structural impact and destabilization in MSH2- MSH6 complex, and hence, the repair mechanism is compromised.
the W764C mutation in MSH2 protein is more deleterious and could be a potential target for the development of novel therapeutics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the missense mutations in MSH2- MSH6 protein complexes can be identified using the in silico methods.
the mutations in the interface of MSH2- MS H6 could have an impact on the DNA repair mechanism.
we can predict deleterious and pathogenic mutations in MSH2 and MSH6 protein complex that can be used in the clinical diagnosis of mismatch repair disorders.
